oliver-cromwell

Oliver Cromwell, the commander of the Parliament's army in the English Civil War, stands in armor with a young page beside him. Robert Walker painted him in 1649, the year the king was executed, and Cromwell later ruled England as Lord Protector.
equestrian-portrait-of-charles-i

King Charles I rides a gray horse in a grand portrait by Anthony van Dyck of about 1637. Van Dyck, the king's court painter, made the short king look tall and noble, and the portrait shows the style of rule that led to the civil war.
charles-i-in-three-positions

Anthony van Dyck painted the face of King Charles I from three sides in 1635 so that the sculptor Bernini in Rome could carve a bust of the king from the picture. It is one of the most famous portraits of an English king.
the-five-eldest-children-of-charles-i

The five eldest children of Charles I, including the future kings Charles II and James II, stand with a huge dog in one of the sweetest royal portraits. Anthony van Dyck painted it in 1637, only a few years before the family was torn apart by civil war.
and-when-did-you-last-see-your-father

A small boy, the son of a Royalist, is questioned by Parliament's officers about where his father is hiding. William Frederick Yeames painted this tense scene from the English Civil War in 1878, and it became one of the most famous pictures in Victorian Britain.
the-proscribed-royalist-1651-john-everett-m

A hiding Royalist soldier in a hollow tree is brought food and secret messages by the girl he loves, who is on the other side of the war. John Everett Millais painted this romantic scene from the English Civil War in 1853.
charles-i-insulted-by-cromwell-s-soldiers
King Charles I sits quietly while his Puritan guards mock him before his trial in 1649. Paul Delaroche painted the king's calm dignity in 1837, and it made viewers sympathize with him.
the-execution-of-king-charles-i

A crowd gathers outside the Banqueting House in London on January 30, 1649, where King Charles I was beheaded, the only time an English king was executed. This print was made around the time of the event.
king-charles-ii

Charles II, who was brought back as king in 1660 after eleven years without a monarch, sits in elegant robes. This portrait was painted around 1665 by John Michael Wright, and Charles was known as the Merry Monarch.
the-battle-of-the-boyne

In July 1690 the Protestant King William III defeated the Catholic King James II at the Battle of the Boyne in Ireland, ending James's hope of getting back his throne. Jan van Huchtenburgh painted this crowded battle in the 1690s.
a-lost-cause-flight-of-king-james-ii

King James II, who had lost his throne in the Glorious Revolution of 1688, waits on the shore for a boat to take him into exile in France. Andrew Carrick Gow painted the sad moment in 1888, 200 years later.
peter-the-great
Tsar Peter the Great strides ahead so fast that his courtiers struggle to keep up in this lively painting, which shows his energy and force of will. Valentin Serov painted it in 1907.
the-victory-at-poltava
In 1709 Peter the Great's army defeated the Swedes under Charles XII at Poltava, a victory that made Russia a great power. Alexander von Kotzebue painted the battle in 1862.
the-battle-of-gangut
In 1714 Peter the Great's new navy won its first big victory over the Swedish fleet at Gangut in the Baltic Sea. Alexey Bogolyubov painted the battle in 1877.
the-battle-of-poltava
A French painter at Peter's court, Pierre-Denis Martin, painted this view of the Battle of Poltava in 1726, only 17 years after it happened. It shows the whole plain with its lines of soldiers.
victory-at-narva

Swedish soldiers charge in a snowstorm at the Battle of Narva in 1700, where young King Charles XII beat the larger Russian army of Peter the Great. Peter lost the battle but learned from it and built a better army. Gustaf Cederström painted it in 1905.
menshikov-in-berezovo

Alexander Menshikov, once Peter the Great's best friend and the second most powerful man in Russia, sits in a hut in Siberia with his family after his fall from power. Vasily Surikov painted this sad scene in 1883.
grand-duchess-sofia-at-the-novodevichy-convent
Peter the Great's half-sister Sofia, who ruled Russia in his place before he took over, was locked in a convent in 1689. Ilya Repin painted her in 1879 looking angry and trapped.
peter-the-great-tsar-of-russia-1672-1725
Peter the Great, in armor, painted by Godfrey Kneller in 1698 while Peter was visiting England to learn about shipbuilding. The young tsar traveled in Europe to bring new ideas back to Russia.
the-foundation-of-st-petersburg
Peter the Great and his companions look over the swamp on the Neva River where he will found Saint Petersburg in 1703, a new capital that was meant to be Russia's window to Europe.
a-reading-of-voltaire-s-tragedy-at-madame-geoffrin-s-sa

A crowd of writers and thinkers listens to a reading in the salon of Madame Geoffrin, one of the places where Enlightenment ideas were discussed, while a bust of Voltaire looks on. Anicet Charles Gabriel Lemonnier painted it in 1812 to show the famous salons of the 1750s.
sir-isaac-newton
Sir Isaac Newton, who explained gravity and the movement of the planets, looks out of this portrait by Godfrey Kneller from 1702. Newton's ideas were a cornerstone of the Enlightenment.
benjamin-franklin
Benjamin Franklin, scientist, printer and American diplomat, in a portrait painted in Paris in 1785 by Joseph-Siffred Duplessis. It is the portrait that was later used for the US hundred-dollar bill.
benjamin-franklin-drawing-electricity-from-the-sky

Benjamin Franklin raises a hand to catch lightning from the sky, while cherubs bring electricity into the room. Benjamin West painted it around 1816 to show Franklin's famous experiment of 1752, which proved lightning is electricity.
frontispiece-of-the-encyclopedie

At the front of the great French Encyclopédie, Truth is unveiled by Reason and Philosophy, with the light of knowledge shining. The Encyclopédie, edited by Diderot, gathered all the Enlightenment's knowledge, and this engraving by Charles-Nicolas Cochin was its frontispiece in 1772.
portrait-of-denis-diderot

Denis Diderot, the editor of the Encyclopédie, which tried to collect all of human knowledge in one set of books. Dmitry Levitzky painted him in 1773, when Catherine the Great invited the philosopher to Russia.
louis-xiv-visiting-the-royal-academy-of-sciences

King Louis XIV visits the Royal Academy of Sciences in Paris in 1671, where telescopes, globes and instruments show how science was becoming an official part of French life. This engraving was made by Sébastien Leclerc in the same year.
alexander-von-humboldt

Alexander von Humboldt, the scientist who explored South America and described the planet as an interconnected whole, sits with his notebooks after a five-year journey. Friedrich Georg Weitsch painted him in 1806.
a-view-of-the-plundering-and-burning-of-the-city-of-gri

British ships and soldiers burn an Acadian settlement on the Saint John River in 1758, during the Seven Years' War. The engraving after the soldier-artist Thomas Davies shows smoke hanging over the water.
the-wounded-montcalm-is-brought-back-to-quebec
The French commander Montcalm, mortally wounded on the Plains of Abraham, is carried back into Quebec City on horseback in 1759. Louis Bombled painted the sad moment in 1900.
lord-clive-meeting-mir-jafar-after-the-battle-of-plasse

After the Battle of Plassey in 1757, Robert Clive of the East India Company meets Mir Jafar, the Indian ruler he helped put in power, in a scene from the global Seven Years' War. Francis Hayman painted it around 1760.
the-battle-of-kunersdorf-1-august-1759

Frederick the Great of Prussia is badly defeated by the Russians and Austrians at the Battle of Kunersdorf on August 1, 1759, in the Seven Years' War, which was fought in Europe, India and North America. Alexander von Kotzebue painted it in 1848.
the-capture-of-the-alcide-and-lys-near-louisbourg-1755
British warships capture the French ships Alcide and Lys off the coast of Canada in 1755, in the sea fight that helped start the Seven Years' War.
the-burning-of-the-prudent-and-capture-of-the-bienfaisa

British sailors set fire to the French warship Prudent in the harbor of Louisbourg in 1758, when the British captured the fortress, a key step toward taking Quebec. This engraving was published in 1771.
george-washington-as-a-virginia-colonel

George Washington, in the red and blue uniform of a Virginia militia colonel, in a portrait painted in 1772 by Charles Willson Peale. Washington had fought in the French and Indian War, the American part of the Seven Years' War.
colonel-bouquet-and-the-return-of-captives-1764

After Pontiac's War, Colonel Henry Bouquet forced the Native nations to hand back the settlers they had taken, and many of the captives, who had grown up with Native families, did not want to leave. This engraving, after Benjamin West, appeared in 1766.
fort-oswego
A British trading fort stands on the shore of Lake Ontario at Oswego, New York, which the French captured in 1756 early in the Seven Years' War. This view is a 19th-century picture of the fort.
the-plains-of-abraham

British boats land at the foot of the cliffs below Quebec in 1759, before the soldiers climbed up to the Plains of Abraham to fight the French. Hervey Smythe, a British officer who served with General Wolfe, made this view of the scene.
the-battle-of-bunker-s-hill

On June 17, 1775, British troops stormed Bunker Hill outside Boston, one of the first big battles of the American Revolution, and the American general Joseph Warren was killed. John Trumbull, who watched the battle from across the river, painted it in 1786.
washington-and-lafayette-at-valley-forge

George Washington and the young French marquis de Lafayette ride through the snow at Valley Forge in the winter of 1777–1778, when the American army nearly starved but became a stronger force. John Ward Dunsmore painted it in 1907.
the-bloody-massacre-perpetrated-in-king-street-boston

British soldiers fire into a crowd in Boston on March 5, 1770, killing five colonists. Paul Revere copied and published this engraving, which made the Boston Massacre famous and helped turn many colonists against Britain.
paul-revere
The silversmith Paul Revere, later famous for his midnight ride in 1775, rests his chin on his hand in front of a gleaming teapot. John Singleton Copley painted him at work in 1768.
the-battle-of-cowpens
American and British cavalry fight in a sword duel at the Battle of Cowpens in South Carolina in 1781, one of the clearest American victories of the Revolution. William Ranney painted it in 1845.
marquis-de-lafayette

The Marquis de Lafayette, a young French nobleman, joined Washington's army at the age of 19 and became a hero of the American Revolution. Ary Scheffer painted this portrait in 1823, when Lafayette toured the United States.
thomas-jefferson
Thomas Jefferson, the writer of the Declaration of Independence and the third president of the United States, was painted by Rembrandt Peale in 1800, the year Jefferson was elected.
george-washington-williamstown-portrait
George Washington, the leader of the American army in the Revolution and first president, in a portrait by Gilbert Stuart painted in 1803. Stuart painted Washington from life and made many copies.
the-passage-of-the-delaware
General George Washington on his horse watches his soldiers cross the icy Delaware River on Christmas night, 1776, before their surprise attack on Trenton. Thomas Sully painted this moment in 1819.
